newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs close lower on persisting bearish mood.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs close lower on persisting bearish mood.

text.p: Persisting jitters about the gloomy prospects dragged the Seoul bourse to a lower close on Tuesday as many investors stuck to the sidelines, brokers said.
The composite index ended 3.77 points lower to a provisional 747.05, after fluctuating between 747.04 and 754.71.
Six of the seven initial public offerings that started trading ended sharply lower on their first day of trading.
"Investors wanted to see something new and positive. But they just stayed away as the market's trend didn't show any change," said Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities.
Volume totalled 19.13 million shares, down from 22.48 million on Monday. Declining stocks far outpaced advancers by 525 to 312, with 176 stocks trading unchanged.
Korea Technology Banking Corp, which newly listed shares on the stock market, closed at its daily upper limit of 21,200 won by gaining 1,200.
Six other new listings closed sharply lower, affected by the weakness of the overall market, brokers said.
"The listings were badly timed as the market has been languishing for a long time," said Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.
Dong Ah Construction closed 100 won higher at 22,300 after rising to a high of 23,100 won in early trading on news that the company was assured of a $5.1 billion Libyan deal.
S1 Corp ended flat at 190,000 won after temporarily rising to 200,000. An S1 official said the company was expected to post a 371 percent rise in this year's net profit.
Brokers predicted the market would remain in the doldrums on Wednesday in absence of any fresh market factor.
The index futures December contracts ended 0.60 points lower at 79.55 while the KOSPI-200 index fell 0.36 points to 78.66.
